CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness, tingling, and pain in left wrist and hand.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presenting with numbness and tingling in the fingers and pain in the left wrist and hand for several months. Symptoms began gradually without clear precipitating cause. Patient notes symptoms are most pronounced at night, with episodes of hand falling asleep that require shaking to restore sensation. Numbness involves all fingers with greater prominence in the thumb and pointer finger, and occasional involvement of the little finger. Denies involvement of right hand. Patient works as a landscaper performing heavy repetitive labor including raking and digging. Associated weakness in left hand manifested by dropping objects due to difficulty feeling them. No prior history of rheumatoid arthritis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupational: Works as a landscaper performing yard work, maintenance, and upkeep of flower beds involving heavy repetitive labor performed consistently. Alcohol: Drinks approximately one to two beers on Friday and Saturday evenings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs normal. Left grip strength reduced compared to right. Sensation to light touch intact bilaterally. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign at wrist with reproduction of jolt or tingling in fingertips.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome presumed secondary to repetitive occupational activities from landscaping work. Activity modification recommended with delegation of repetitive heavy labor to employees for approximately two weeks. Patient to wear wrist splint. Ibuprofen 600 mg every six hours prescribed. EMG study to be ordered to measure electrical impulses in fingers. Follow-up office visit scheduled in two weeks to assess response to conservative treatment and determine need for additional diagnostic testing or surgical intervention.
